title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the Medical Leadership Competence Scale among residents
content:
by Di Xue, Aijun Zhu, Zhijun Wu, Huaijie Yang, Jian Zheng, Li Li, Min Hu, Man Hu

Objective

To translate the Medical Leadership Competence Scale (MeLeCoS) into Chinese, culturally adapt it, test its reliability and validity among resident physicians, and provide a tool for assessing resident physicians’ medical leadership competence.

Methods

We translated, back-translated, and culturally adapted the scale using Brislin’s method to form the Chinese version of the Medical Leadership Competence Scale. In Phase 1, we used cluster sampling to conduct a questionnaire survey among 242 resident physicians at a national-level standardized residency training base in the Yichang area from March to April 2025, and we used these data for exploratory factor analysis. In Phase 2, we selected another 210 resident physicians (non-overlapping sample) from July to September 2026 and conducted a questionnaire survey for confirmatory factor analysis. The initial confirmatory factor analysis yielded unsatisfactory results. After discussion within the research team, we revised the scale. We then used the revised scale to collect data again from the same respondents in Sample 2, recovered 207 valid questionnaires, and conducted a second confirmatory factor analysis.

Results

Exploratory factor analysis extracted five common factors, with a cumulative variance contribution rate of 71.031%. The average scale-level content validity index (S-CVI/Ave) was 0.982, and the item-level content validity index (I-CVI) ranged from 0.833 to 1.000. The critical ratio method showed that the CR values of all items reached a significant level (p < 0.001). In the item-total correlation analysis, the correlation coefficients between all items and the total scale score ranged from r = 0.436 to 0.807. The initial confirmatory factor analysis model fit indices were: χ2/df = 2.745, CFI = 0.830, TLI = 0.817, IFI = 0.831, RMSEA = 0.092, and SRMR = 0.0980. After scale revision, the scale retained 29 items and 5 factors. The revised confirmatory factor analysis model fit indices were: χ2/df = 2.094, CFI = 0.864, TLI = 0.849, IFI = 0.866, RMSEA = 0.073, and SRMR = 0.0724. The Cronbach’s α coefficient of the revised total scale was 0.941, and the Cronbach’s α coefficients of the dimensions were 0.817, 0.905, 0.791, 0.733, and 0.753. The split-half reliability was 0.890.

Conclusion

The Chinese version of MeLeCoS shows good internal consistency reliability and content validity, while evidence for its factor structure and construct validity requires further verification. This scale can be used for the preliminary assessment of medical leadership among resident physicians, provides a preliminary tool for assessing medical leadership in standardized residency training in China, and facilitates investigations of resident physicians’ leadership and their self-reflection.
author: Di Xue
